title: Alex Warren’s ‘Ordinary’ Lands Third Month at No. 1 on Top Gabb Music Songs Chart
summary: The song joins “Die With a Smile” and “Your Way’s Better” as previous three-month leaders.
contentText:
Alex Warren ’s “Ordinary” becomes the third song to lead the Top Gabb Music Songs chart for three months, stringing together its third frame in a row to kick off 2026 via the January 2026 list.

Related

Billboard has partnered with Gabb Wireless, a phone company for kids and teens, to present a monthly chart tracking on-demand streams via its Gabb Music platform. Gabb Music offers a vast catalog of songs, all of which are selected by the Gabb team to include only kid- and teen-appropriate content. Gabb Music streams are not currently factored into any other Billboard charts.

Warren’s run with “Ordinary” now equals Lady Gaga and Bruno Mars ’ “Die With a Smile” and Forrest Frank ’s “Your Way’s Better” as three-month No. 1s on the chart, which was first published in October 2024. Both “Die With a Smile” and “Your Way’s Better” also achieved their rules consecutively.

“Ordinary” has remained a force for Warren on the weekly Billboard Hot 100 . Following its 10-week run at No. 1 last week, it’s been within the top 10 every week since the Jan. 10-dated tally, including one week (Jan. 17) at No. 2.

Its closest competitor on Top Gabb Music Songs is a newcomer to the top 10: Djo ’s “End of Beginning,” which zooms 17-2 in its second month on the ranking. Released in 2022 and first achieving virality in 2024 via shortform video platforms such as TikTok, “End of Beginning” has surged yet again around the release of the final season of Netflix’s Stranger Things , on which Joe Keery — who records as Djo — is in a starring role.

“End of Beginning” snagged a new peak of No. 6 on the Hot 100 in mid-January and topped the Hot Rock & Alternative Songs chart for two weeks.

The month’s top debut — one of just two for January — belongs to Josiah Queen , whose “Demons” bows at No. 10. That’s two songs for Queen on the latest tally, with “Dusty Bibles” reentering the ranking at No. 19.

“Demons” became Queen’s highest debut yet on Hot Christian Songs upon its release, bowing at No. 4 on the Jan. 31-dated chart. It’s only been bested in overall rank by “Dusty Bibles,” which peaked at No. 3 last July.

Ella Langley ’s “Choosin’ Texas” is the other debut of the month, starting at No. 24, marking her first appearance on Top Gabb Music Songs. Langley has spent one week at No. 1 on the Hot 100, topping the Feb. 14-dated tally.
